newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-WHITE SOX' MOUTON OUT 3-6 WEEKS WITH FACIAL FRACTURE.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-WHITE SOX' MOUTON OUT 3-6 WEEKS WITH FACIAL FRACTURE.

text.p: Chicago White Sox outfielder Lyle Mouton will be out three to six weeks with a facial fracture after colliding with teammate Dave Martinez in the fifth inning of Sunday's 8-5 win over the Oakland Athletics.

Mouton was playing right field when he and Martinez ran into each other while chasing George Williams' fly ball. Both players remained on the ground for several minutes. A stretcher was brought out but not used.
Mouton, who turns 28 on Tuesday, was taken to a hospital, where doctors diagnosed his injury as a broken zygomatic arch on the right side of face. Surgery is likely, team officials said.
Martinez remained in the game before leaving for a pinch-hitter in the bottom of the fifth.
Mouton and Martinez, who suffered a mild concussion, were to remain hospitalized overnight.
"He's hurt and that's part of the game," Chicago manager Terry Bevington said of Mouton. "He'll be back in three to six weeks and our team just needs to move on."
Mouton was placed on the 15-day disabled list after the game and the White Sox recalled outfielder Mike Cameron from Triple-A Nashville.
Mouton is hitting .333 with with two homers and seven RBI in 22 games. Martinez is batting .282 in 31 games with two homers and 15 RBI.
